newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares rise, with more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares rise, with more gains expected.

text.p: Danish share prices followed foreign paper up on Monday and dealers said that the market could continue to rise on Tuesday.

"There is a strongly positive tone to the market today that I would put down mostly to overseas developments. We are rising at the same tempo as the U.S. market and it looks as if it will continue tomorrow," one trader said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.71 point to 120.54 and the KFX September future rose 0.60 point to 120.55 with 166 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Total bourse turnover was a modest 813 million crowns.
The dealer added, however, that the Danish market was highly subject to foreign market movements and with no firm direction of its own.
Thursday's U.S. producer price data and Friday's CPI numbers would have a strong influence on Danish share prices as would domestic bond yields, he added.

Among the day's main gainers was EAC, which rose 2.5 percent to 123 crowns. On August 27 the shipping and trading group reported first-half 1996 profits up from the same period last year and above market expectations.
